    Construction

    The C-75A's small, single-pickup sibling, after the compact electric archtops of the late fifties: the same faceted Port Orford cedar top as the Amicus over a maple core: rim and flat back in one piece, pocketed from the top face of a 2 in blank down to a 3/16 in floor, with solid neck and tail blocks and a pillar under each pickguard post. 2 in deep at the rim, at a 24 in scale like a Jaguar, with 20 frets, so the neck joins at about the 15th fret.

    Soundholes are triangles, one each side of the bridge, each a scaled-down copy of the facet it is cut into and sized to the Amicus slots' open area. One neck pickup, body mounted: a gold foil in the P-90 soapbar footprint on a black riser shaped to the top. Controls on the top, Jaguar-style: volume, two on-off-on slide switches (bass cut, treble cut) and the jack on a nickel plate shaped to the lower treble facet.

    A painted top in aged computer white (milk paint, the C-75's white option), with single-ply white binding; the maple core and the maple neck are dyed black, and the headstock face is black. Red truss rod cover. The tailpiece is the Amicus stainless plate, unchanged: the R shares the Amicus body, top and bridge height, so it drops onto the same four tail-block screws. A black pickguard on three nickel standoffs carries the insignia in white.
